passage:
Every month, the school counselor placed a blue envelope in each classroom. Students could write worries and put them inside. They did not have to write their names.
Some wrote about tests. Some wrote about friends. Some wrote only one sentence: "I feel tired."
The counselor read the notes and planned class talks based on common problems. When many students wrote about sleep, she gave a lesson on rest. When many wrote about friendship, she taught ways to say sorry and set boundaries.
The blue envelope did not solve every problem, but it gave quiet students a voice.
Sometimes the first step to helping people is creating a safe way for them to speak.
